quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When there are two hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Your car has an Anti-Lock Braking System and loses traction on a slippery road. What should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal and hold it. Steer out of danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System will pump the brakes for you automatically. Pumping the brakes yourself or releasing pressure will turn off the system.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right and slow down. Check for oncoming traffic. This helps the passing vehicle move back into the right lane safely and quickly.

questions.question: You see this sign above your lane. What does it mean?

options.text: You can either continue or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the freeway and form a ramp. You must either change lanes to continue through, or exit the freeway.

questions.question: When can you pass safely on a two-lane street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You need all three conditions to pass safely: a clear view ahead, enough time to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle capable of passing speed. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the emergency vehicle is not headed toward you.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no traffic control device, yield to the vehicle on your right.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Held safely by a strong adult.
Standing on the floor in the back.
They are too small to be hurt in an accident.
Never standing—they must be properly fastened in a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never standing—they must be properly fastened in a seat.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats or proper safety belts. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use proper safety seats for children.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track. When can you proceed?

options.text: When you can see clearly down all tracks.
As soon as the train passes.
After you stop on the first track and look around.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see clearly down all tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not move until you have a clear view of all tracks. Another train may be approaching even after the first one passes.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to upcoming food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of driving hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not startle it.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What does an orange sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is present.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: Why is it important to leave space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your vehicle and others so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Wait until the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians, then you can proceed.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign if there is no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the intersection at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop until the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians have time to get out of your way.
Honk your horn to let traffic and pedestrians know to move.
Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. It is against the law not to stop.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing ahead, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop at railroad crossing signs. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not drive around the gate.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a high blood alcohol level can
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving ability suffers. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green left turn arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing left means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you about railroad crossings ahead. Slow down and be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign means a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. This helps you stay in your lane, keep control of your vehicle, and react to unexpected situations.
